title: K-flat descent of a supplied coherent module pullback structure
statement: Let $g:T\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], recorded derived pullback $L=Lg^*$ [def-pc-derived-pullback], and recorded derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Fix an additive functor $F$ identified on objects and arrows with tensor-formula module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], a strong monoidal structure $m_F$ on F, and a left-derived counit $\epsilon:Q_hL\to K(F)Q_h$. Suppose supplied isomorphisms $\varphi_{P,N}:F\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes N)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(FP\otimes FN)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] are natural in both complexes, act on every summand by the inverse tensorator of $m_F$, and make $\epsilon_{P\otimes N};Q(\varphi_{P,N})$ invertible whenever P,N are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Then there is a strong monoidal structure m on L such that for all such P,N, $\mu_m(QP,QN);L(\mu_Q(P,N));\epsilon_{P\otimes N};Q(\varphi_{P,N})=(\epsilon_P\otimes\epsilon_N);\mu_Q(FP,FN)$. All underived coherence, counit, and total-complex comparisons are inputs; the conclusion supplies only their coherent derived descent.

proof.text: Work first on K-flat representatives. The supplied F is the recorded termwise pullback, so it preserves K-flatness. Tensor products of K-flat complexes are K-flat. The derived counit of any left-derived presentation agrees, up to the unique isomorphism of left-derived functors, with the K-flat computation of the recorded pullback, so its components are invertible on K-flat objects. Localization tensorators are invertible on K-flat pairs in the recorded derived monoidal construction.

proof.text: For a K-flat pair set A=L(mu_Q(P,N)), B=epsilon_{P tensor N};Q(phi), and C=(epsilon_P tensor epsilon_N);mu_Q(FP,FN). Define the tensorator by C;B^{-1};A^{-1}; it is invertible and satisfies mu;A;B=C. Replace arbitrary arguments by K-flat resolutions. Naturality of epsilon and phi makes this assignment commute with comparison quasi-isomorphisms, and localization of the resolving class therefore gives a well-defined natural tensorator on all derived objects.

proof.text: Resolve three arguments by K-flat complexes. Precompose the two associativity composites by every triple summand inclusion; the given summand formula for phi reduces equality to the associativity law of m_F, so it holds before and after localization. The structure sheaf in degree zero is K-flat, and F sends it to the target unit by m_F. Use the inverse unit counit and that unit isomorphism to give the derived unit. On summands, the two derived unit diagrams are exactly the unit diagrams of m_F. Descend their equality and package the invertible tensorator and unit as CoreMonoidal. The equation remains the defining equation from the K-flat construction.
